extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: CONTEXTUAL is a context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for large multimodal model evaluation. It covers eight real-world scenarios with text-rich images: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes. Each instance contains a human-written instruction and a human-written ground-truth response, requiring context-sensitive joint reasoning over textual and visual cues.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng (University of California Los Angeles)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources: LAION-5B (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract categories via CLIP-retrieval keyword search), Rico Dataset (for Application Usage), Open WebText Initiative website screenshots (for Web Usage), and existing VQA dataset test sets (InfographicVQA for Infographic, STVQA and ESTVQA for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes). Instructions and responses were human-written by the authors following annotation guidelines.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from: LAION-5B (via CLIP-retrieval UI keyword search), Rico Dataset (66,000 distinct UI screens from 9,300 Android apps), Open WebText Initiative website screenshots, InfographicVQA dataset test set, STVQA dataset test set, and ESTVQA dataset test set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories: manual filtering to guarantee suitability for annotation. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes: heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR to detect text, then selecting the top 500 images with the highest number of words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 - image shortlisting and filtering. Stage 2 - authors divided into two groups, each annotating four categories following provided annotation guidelines to create instruction-response pairs. Stage 3 - MTurk workers verified correctness of each sample (96% found correct); incorrect samples filtered out; each author group then reviewed samples created by the other group to ensure guideline adherence and filter low-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human evaluation, each model response was shown to three human annotators independently who decided if the predicted response was acceptable. The majority vote among the three annotators was used as the final decision. 96% of dataset samples were verified as correctly annotated by MTurk workers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators mainly from the US.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples (validation set) with reference responses will be released publicly; reference responses for the remaining 406 samples will be kept hidden. A continuously updated leaderboard with recent LMMs is maintained.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to help evaluate and improve LMMs for real-world applications such as assisting the visually impaired in navigating text-rich scenes. The authors note awareness that existing multimodal models can generate harmful responses despite safeguard filters, and that linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses may vary across social groups.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human annotators are mainly from the US, which may introduce linguistic and cultural bias in the human baseline and evaluation. The authors acknowledge that results may differ with annotators from more diverse regions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains only 506 instances. Human annotators are mainly from the US, limiting linguistic diversity. Open models lag behind proprietary models, partly due to lack of diverse visual contexts in training data. Synthetic data generation for context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning is challenging and model-generated instructions may be easier for GPT-based models to solve.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking/evaluation (testing) of large multimodal models on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning. It can also be used for fine-grained analysis of model capabilities across visual contexts, and as a leaderboard benchmark for recent LMMs.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: CONTEXTUAL comprises images sourced from six different sources. Firstly, we obtain images for the Time, Shopping, Navigation & Abstract categories from the LAION-5B. Secondly, we source images for the Application Usage category from the Rico Dataset. Thirdly, we scrape the website links made available by the Open WebText Initiative and collect screenshots for the Web Usage category. Lastly, we acquire images from the test sets of existing VQA datasets.

However, for Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, we perform heuristic-based filtering. Specifically, we employ a PaddleOCR (paddlepadle, 2023) to detect the text in the image. Subsequently, we select the top 500 images with the highest number of words.
